title: How Ann-Sophie Schälicke Redefines Inclusive Fashion With Clo
description:
Discover the story of Ann-Sophie Schälicke, a Germany-based designer redefining inclusive fashion with her brand A. Schaelicke. Through her participation in the Design Academy ADAPT program co-hosted by VORN – The Berlin Fashion Hub and Zalando, she discovered CLO, which enabled her to create adaptive designs for all body types. For Ann-Sophie, CLO isn’t just a tool; it’s the key to making her inclusive vision a reality.

Learn more about Design Academy ADAPT program: https://vorn-hub.com/design-academy-adapt-1
Learn more about A. Schaelicke: https://www.instagram.com/a.schaelicke/?hl=en
transcript: Hi, my name is Anne-Sophie Schellekern and I'm a German-based fashion designer dedicated to inclusive fashion. I saw the lack in the market, the accessibility, and the gaps not only in the products but also in the representation of the whole industry. And I wanted to close the gap and make shows with purpose so it's not just fabric, it's like an alley in your everyday life that supports and empowers you. My first step into adaptive fashion was my inclusive graduate collection in 2023. The name is Spotlight. I chose the name because I wanted to have the disabled community take center stage. I could stand in the spotlight. It stands out because of its innovative closures. I used magnets and bold font prints and futuristic silhouettes. The Design Academy is an educational program co-hosted by Vaughan, the Berlin Fashion Hub, and Zalando, the third edition, focused on creating innovation in adaptive fashion. The program gave me the opportunity to connect with like-minded designers and incredible industry experts and gave me the right tools for my work. And it's also where I discovered Claw. The most helpful tool of Claw for me is the virtual try-on with the avatar and the pose customization and the fabric simulation. So it allows me to adjust the body, types of my customers. So for example, seated position for wheelchair users. And the simulation allows me to adjust the fit for these specific needs. I use magnets and a special pattern cutting for the body position so that it looks flattering while standing and also while sitting. So for me, it shows more. And just the software, it's a tool that empowers me to design in a way that it aligns with my physical strengths. I don't need to use physical strength anymore and only focus on designing. Even in my most toughest moments when I was hospitalized, I could work on my adaptive pieces with Claw. So the tool gave me the freedom and the flexibility to do my work from anywhere. Claw has given me the tools to bring my vision to life with more precision and creativity. And I'm excited to see where it evolves in the future of adaptive fashion.
